D010-D005_h001.question:
Lately, things have been… off. For the past two months, it’s been like someone hit the fast-forward button on my brain. I snap at my wife and the tellers for the smallest things, just an explosion of anger. I can't sit still; I'm constantly pacing my office, can't focus on reports, just need to *do* something, anything. My thoughts race so fast, and my words come out in a jumble, I know I'm speaking too quickly for anyone to keep up. I've also been making some pretty hefty purchases, things we don't really need, draining our savings without much thought.

But that’s not even the strangest part. I keep noticing things, like the news anchors are talking directly to me, or even the posters on the street are sending me messages. And sometimes, I feel as if there are ants crawling all over my skin, even when there's nothing there.

Before all this, for about five months, it was like I was walking through mud. I couldn’t feel anything – no joy from my kids, no satisfaction from closing a big deal at the bank. Everything was just... flat. Even picking out what tie to wear in the morning felt like an impossible task. It was crippling, really. I just don't know what's going on with me.
D010-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

But then that faded, and for the past two months, it’s been the opposite. Everything just feels… flat. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my grandkids. Mornings are the worst. Sometimes I just lie there, wishing I wouldn't wake up, though I'd never do anything about it. Even talking feels like a chore, like my words are stuck in molasses. And it's odd, but sometimes I smell faint burning plastic, even when there's nothing on fire. My wife says it's my imagination. The strangest thing, though, is this feeling that the lady from apartment 3B... that she’s somehow in love with me. She's always looking my way, giving me little smiles. I just know it.
